raw_text:
This .NET 10/C# 14 codebase, **csharparr**, is a Transmission RPC-compatible put.io/*arr proxy (Sonarr/Radarr/Whisparr) that monitors transfers, downloads files, and manages imports.

Stack: ASP.NET Core, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience + Polly, System.CommandLine, Tomlyn, xUnit/Moq/FluentAssertions. Write concise, idiomatic C#; prefer simplicity, focused/minimal solutions, and avoid over-engineering.

Structure:
```
Commands/        # CLI command handlers
Configuration/   # TOML parsing/validation
Download/        # orchestration/workers
Http/            # Transmission RPC controllers
Services/        # Put.io/Arr clients
Program.cs       # DI entry point
tests/Csharparr.Tests/{Configuration,Download,Http,Services,Integration}/
```

Conventions: PascalCase public types/members; camelCase locals/parameters; `_camelCase` private fields; `I`-prefixed interfaces; file-scoped namespaces; records for DTOs/immutable data; pattern matching; nullable reference types; top-level `Program.cs`; `[]` for empty collections; `Lock` (not `object`); primary constructors when appropriate; raw string literals. Use `var` when obvious, explicit types for clarity, expression-bodied simple members, `?.`, `??`, `??=`, and interpolation (except logs). Keep methods focused and under ~50 lines when possible.

All I/O-bound operations must be async. Always pass `CancellationToken` through the call chain; use `cancellationToken = default` for optional parameters; suffix async methods with `Async`. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log cancellation at Debug, not Error.

Use `BackgroundService` for long-running tasks, bounded `Channel<T>` for producer-consumer work, track background tasks, and periodically clean completed tasks/resources/expired entries. Use thread-safe collections or protect shared state with `Lock`.

Use typed clients (`AddHttpClient<IPutioClient, PutioClient>`) for service APIs, named clients (`AddHttpClient("ArrClient")`) for shared configurations, per-operation timeouts, and `IHttpClientFactory` in background services. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (not deprecated `Polly.Extensions.Http`); configure exponential-backoff jitter retry and circuit breakers. Retry network errors (`HttpRequestException`), `TimeoutException`, `TaskCanceledException`, and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.

Register configuration as singleton; use interfaces for all services; register typed clients with interfaces; use factories for dynamic clients:
```
builder.Services.AddSingleton(config);
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IPutioClient, PutioClient>(...);
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IArrClientFactory, ArrClientFactory>();
builder.Services.AddHostedService<DownloadManager>();
```
Always register services with their interfaces, not concrete types. Test concurrent resolution and DI integration (`tests/Integration/`).

Use exceptions for exceptional cases, not control flow. Create `PutioException`/`ArrClientException`. Include truncated (500 chars) response bodies in HTTP errors. Log `BrokenCircuitException` at Debug, socket errors as Warning without full stack trace, and continue other operations when one service fails.

Use structured logging with message templates, not string interpolation. Levels: Debug operational details; Information startup/transfers/completions; Warning recovered/expected failures; Error attention-required failures; Fatal terminating errors. Override `Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime: Information`. Don't log expected cancellation/circuit-breaker conditions at Error.

Testing: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`. Test happy/error paths; mock HTTP/external dependencies; verify DI resolution:
```
public void CanResolveTransmissionController()
using var factory = new WebApplicationFactory<Program>();
var scope = factory.Services.CreateScope();
var controller = scope.ServiceProvider.GetService<TransmissionController>();
controller.Should().NotBeNull();
```

Use Tomlyn; validate configuration at startup with detailed errors, providing all errors at once. Required fields: `username`, `password` (HTTP basic auth), `instance_name` (3-10 alphanumeric), `instance_folder_id`, `download_directory`, `putio.api_key`; at least one Arr service.

Implement Transmission RPC compatibility; use `[Route("/transmission/rpc")]`; preserve JSON property names (`PropertyNamingPolicy = null`); provide `/health` returning simple 200 OK. Use multi-stage Dockerfile, non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, and support linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64.

Don't add features or refactor beyond what's requested.
Don't add comments, docstrings, or type annotations to unchanged code.
Don't create helpers or abstractions for one-time operations.
Don't add error handling for scenarios that can't happen.
Don't use `Polly.Extensions.Http` (deprecated)—use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`
Don't log at Error level for expected conditions (cancellation, circuit breaker)
Don't use string interpolation in log messages
Don't register concrete types when interfaces exist
